newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ$1 bln Govt savings could drop dollar, rates- BT.
newsitem.headline: NZ$1 bln Govt savings could drop dollar, rates- BT.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar and interest rates could drop significantly if the government found NZ$1 billion in savings, according to a report by Bankers Trust Research released on Friday.
The report was commissioned by the Manufacturers' Federation.

ManFed chief executive Simon Arnold said the report found that the dollar could drop by four percent on a trade weighted basis or interest rates fall by two percent or some combination in between if NZ$1 billion in savings were found.

The report said the impact of the coalition government's agreement was estimated to have added significantly to interest rates and the exchange rate already, compared to what it would have been if the government's December Economic and Fiscal Update (DEFU) had been adhered to.
"What we advocate is that the timing for the proposed Government spend be rescheduled and the existing expenditure be stringently reviewed," Arnold said.
The coalition government has announced extra spending of $1.2 bilion in the 1997/98 year but has deferred $1 billion in tax cuts set for July 1, 1997 by the previous National government.
"Spending by the coalition when capacity in the non-tradeable or service sector is at a premium is just fuelling inflation," Arnold said.
Manfed has consistently urged the government to curb its spending to take the pressure off a rising dollar.

He said the planned extra spending would reduce job opportunities and ramp up home mortgage interest rates. It would not have the same impact as tax cuts for individuals because they would save at least part of those.
"For this reason the NZ$1 billion tax cut deferred for 1997/98 would have the same impact on inflation as a $700 million spending increase," Arnold said.

In its report Bankers Trust said while monetary reaction to the fiscal stimulus would not be permanent, the costs imposed on domestic producers could be significant, and the long term growth path may be affected.
Bankers Trust said its estimates reflected modelling results rather than economic forecasts.

The coalition has promised a binding referendum on a compulsory superannuation scheme. The report assumes no compulsory scheme, but BT said if the referendum opted for one it would offset the effects of the deferred tax cuts.
